official_immigration_source_name: Visas and Permit Criteria – Cook Islands Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration
cross_check_source_name: Immigration FAQs – Cook Islands Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration
review_notes: The Ministry states NZ/Australia passport holders receive 90 days on arrival and all other passport holders receive 31 days on arrival. Bangladesh ordinary passports fall in the latter group. The International Visitor Visa/Permit is issued on arrival without pre-travel application. Arrival requirements include six-month passport validity, onward travel, accommodation, sufficient funds, good character and acceptable health. The current October 2026 FAQ gives NZD115 for a 31-day extension; the 2023 regulation schedule is older and is not used for the current extension amount.

visa_requirement_type: Sponsored visitor entry permit (not a visa)

review_notes: Bangladesh is not listed among American Samoa's visa-waiver countries. A holder of a valid U.S. visa/green card may qualify for the separate US Visa 30-Day route. The Department of Legal Affairs page permits a one-time USD50 extension, while the Visitors Bureau table says the Other 30-Day permit cannot be extended; extension availability is explicitly flagged as conflicting.

official_immigration_source_name: Visa Waiver Program – U.S. Department of State
cross_check_source_name: Bangladesh Reciprocity Schedule – U.S. Department of State
review_notes: The U.S. Department of State lists the 12 Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program nationalities; Bangladesh is not included. The general U.S. Visa Waiver Program list also excludes Bangladesh, so a B-1/B-2 visitor visa is required for tourism. The Bangladesh reciprocity schedule lists B-1/B-2 as single-entry, three-month validity, with no reciprocity issuance fee. The MRV application fee is USD185. Since 21 January 2026, Bangladesh is on the U.S. visa-bond list: if the consular officer directs, the bond is USD10,000, USD15,000 or USD20,000; it is not a visa fee and does not guarantee issuance. Bond holders must enter and exit through commercial air ports of entry.

maximum_permitted_stay: Up to 3 months per 6 months, subject to the territorial visa.
passport_validity_rule: Valid at least 3 months after departure; issued within 10 years.
transit_rule: Bangladesh nationals need a French airport-transit visa for transit through France/overseas territories, unless exempt.
application_channel: Apply via France-Visas for a territory-specific short-stay visa; submit to the French consular authority.
application_fee: Territory-specific visa fee not stated in the reviewed order; confirm at lodgement.
processing_time: No SLA in the territorial order; check French consular appointment and processing guidance.
required_documents: Passport meeting the 3-month, 2-blank-page and under-10-year rules; territory-specific visa; supporting documents generated by France-Visas for the individual case.
official_immigration_source_name: Arrêté du 22 juillet 2011 relatif aux documents et visas exigés pour l'entrée des étrangers en Nouvelle-Calédonie – Légifrance
review_notes: The current New Caledonia entry order sets a short-stay limit of up to three months in any six-month period and lists the nationalities exempt from the visa requirement in Annex II. Bangladesh is not on that exemption list, so a Bangladeshi ordinary-passport holder requires a territory-specific short-stay visa. The passport must be valid at least three months beyond departure, have two blank pages and have been issued within the previous ten years. A Schengen short-stay visa alone does not authorize entry into New Caledonia. Bangladesh is listed for French airport-transit visa purposes; transit through mainland France or the overseas territory must be checked separately.

maximum_permitted_stay: 14 days short-term; long-term visitor visa up to 6 months, extendable.
passport_validity_rule: Valid travel document; no minimum residual validity stated in the policy.
return_ticket_rule: Short-term visitor must arrive and depart on the same vessel.

application_channel: 14 days or less: apply on arrival; over 14 days: apply before travel through Pitcairn Immigration.

processing_time: No SLA published; long-term applications should be lodged well before travel.
required_documents: Valid travel document; combined immigration/biosecurity declaration; insurance; evidence of funds or sponsor. Long-term route requires application form, medical certificate, chest X-ray and police certificates.
official_immigration_source_name: Immigration – Official Website of the Government of the Pitcairn Islands
review_notes: The Pitcairn Government's current immigration policy applies to all visitors. Short-term visitors staying 14 days or less may obtain a visitor visa on arrival, provided they arrive and depart on the same vessel and satisfy health, character, financial and insurance requirements. Longer stays require a visitor visa before travel; the public government page lists NZD150 and validity up to six months, with possible extension. The short-term fee amount is not stated on the public page and is left unspecified.

application_channel: Apply to Tokelau Support Services at least 1 month before travel; appropriate village approval required.

review_notes: Tokelau Government Support Services states that all foreign visitors must obtain an entry permit and receive approval from the appropriate village before travel. The published guidance asks visitors to contact Support Services at least one month before the intended visit. The authority describes this as an entry permit, not a visa. The reviewed public guidance does not specify a fee, maximum stay or complete supporting-document checklist; those fields are intentionally left blank.
